links.outcome: Temporal performance drift and dataset drift of cardiac surgery mortality prediction models
links.effect: Strong evidence of decrease in overall performance across all models (p < 0.0001); all models decreased in at least 3 of 5 metrics; sharp drift periods mirrored performance decreases.
links.quote: There was a strong evidence of decrease in overall performance across all models (p < 0.0001).

links.outcome: Loss of model accuracy over time relative to initial validation
links.effect: Performance of ML and ES II declined over time after temporal split; ML remained superior to ES II; regular assessment and modification suggested.
links.quote: ML performance decreases over time due to dataset drift, but remains superior to ES II.

unlisted_practices: Consensus composite metric (Clinical Effective Metric) combining discrimination, calibration, clinical usefulness and accuracy for model comparison
Variable importance drift detection as a signal of dataset drift

links.effect: Xgboost CEM 0.728 95CI: 0.728-0.729 and Random Forest CEM 0.727 95CI 0.727-0.728 were best overall.
links.quote: Xgboost (CEM 0.728 95CI: 0.728-0.729) and Random Forest (CEM 0.727 95CI 0.727-0.728) were the best overall performing models both temporally and non-temporally.
